title: Friend Pitch Night Studio
oneLiner: A playful event kit that helps friends pitch their single friends offline without turning the night into another dating-app profile review.
targetUser: Gen Z and millennial friend groups, singles-event hosts, community organizers, and creators making offline dating events more social.
keyUx: Friends build a short pitch deck for one single person, choose the vibe, add conversation-safe details, set boundaries, and generate a live event slide plus shareable invite card.
requiredUiSections: Pitch subject consent and boundary check
Friend quote collector with green/yellow/red detail labels
Vibe selector for dinner-party, run-club, karaoke, book-club, and chaotic PowerPoint night
Slide builder with strengths, ideal first setting, and do-not-say-this guardrails
Audience reaction meter and match-intro queue
Event host control panel for timing, slides, and opt-out
Shareable invite card and post-night reflection

externalSignalRefs.source: Axios, singles choosing bars and events over dating apps
externalSignalRefs.observed: Singles are burned out from swiping and moving toward run clubs, dinners, friend pitches, and lower-pressure in-person formats.

externalSignalRefs.source: Reddit r/hingeapp, repeated no-match profile review posts
externalSignalRefs.observed: Users ask strangers for profile reviews after premium tiers and no results, showing shame and uncertainty around self-presentation.

stitchPrompt: Create a responsive web app prototype for "Friend Pitch Night Studio," a playful offline dating event kit where friends pitch their single friends with consent, boundaries, and humor. Include: pitch subject consent and boundary check, friend quote collector, vibe selector, slide builder, audience reaction meter, match-intro queue, event host control panel, shareable invite card, and post-night reflection. Design direction: use the playful-experimental profile with polished social-event energy, bold presentation-night visuals, tactile slide controls, expressive but readable colors, and meme-ready share cards; it should feel fun and portfolio-worthy while making consent and boundaries obvious.
